# Surface accuracy on DrivAerML {#sec-surface}

```{python}
#| label: setup-surface
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"

# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 wide, 12 layers, 256 slices, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4), scored by
# the fleet scorer and reduced in results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json; the training-car ladder below 435 cars is the
# re-run of the same rungs (results/refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json); the baseline rows are the released
# GeoTransolver and Transolver lanes of the reporting protocol.
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
ref_seeds = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["seeds"]
RB = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json"); RBS = RB["summary"]; RBX = RB["learning_curve_exponents"]
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")
def ladder_rung(n):
    gt = {"1e-3": RBS[f"gt256|n{n}"], "3e-3": RBS[f"gt256_lr3e3|n{n}"]}
    glab = min(gt, key=lambda k: gt[k]["mean"])
    return dict(isla=RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["seeds"], gt=gt[glab]["seeds"], gt_rate=glab, t=RBS[f"transolver256|n{n}"]["seeds"])
A = P2["arms"]
gt435 = {"1e-3": A["gt_unit_lr1e3"], "3e-3": A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]}
g435lab = min(gt435, key=lambda k: gt435[k]["pressure_mean"])
runs = lambda a: [v["pressure_l2"] for v in a["per_run"].values()]
CARS = {n: ladder_rung(n) for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)}
CARS[435] = dict(isla=ref_seeds("isla_r1|dr435"), gt=runs(gt435[g435lab]), gt_rate=g435lab, t=runs(A["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]))
car_ratio = {n: (mean(r["gt"]) / mean(r["isla"]), mean(r["t"]) / mean(r["isla"])) for n, r in CARS.items()}
# the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512, the 24-layer depth variant and the rate control, all at 435 cars; step time
# and memory of every configuration at 200,000 tokens from the reference cost sweep
GT512 = ref_seeds("gt_w512|dr435"); R2 = ref_seeds("isla_r2|dr435"); R1_LR = ref_seeds("isla_r1_lr1e3|dr435")
CS = {r["arm"]: r for r in J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"] if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
COST = {k: (statistics.median(CS[a]["step_ms"]), CS[a]["peak_allocated_gib"]) for k, a in
        (("isla", "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"), ("r2", "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused"), ("gt", "geotransolver_256"),
         ("gt512", "geotransolver_512"), ("t", "transolver_256"))}
ratio = lambda a, b, i: COST[a][i] / COST[b][i]   # cost ratios are baseline ÷ ISLA, two decimals everywhere
PC = J("drivaer435_percase_2026-09-23.json")  # per-car anatomy of the 435-car standing (ISLA against GeoTransolver-512)
```

```{python}
#| label: para-surface-lede
#| output: asis
g435 = car_ratio[435][0]; g512 = mean(GT512) / mean(CARS[435]["isla"])
print(f"**At full data on the DrivAerML Surface task ISLA leads GeoTransolver at its recipe width by {pct(g435)} and ties its "
      f"parameter match, GeoTransolver-512, which costs {ratio('gt512', 'isla', 0):.2f}x ISLA's step time and "
      f"{ratio('gt512', 'isla', 1):.2f}x its memory; below about one hundred training cars GeoTransolver leads.** "
      "The standings are @tbl-scoreboard-435 (435 cars, with cost) and @tbl-scoreboard-200k with @fig-drivaerml-ladder "
      "(the training-car ladder). Protocol: @sec-protocol, 200,000 sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, two seeds, each "
      "architecture at its own best learning rate; the metric is the area-weighted relative L2 of surface pressure in "
      "float32 over the 48 validation cars (@sec-metrics), and every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, so a value above one "
      "favors ISLA.")
```

## The 435-car standing {#sec-scoreboard-200k}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-435
#| output: asis
r = CARS[435]
def cell(v):
    return f"{mean(v):.4f} ({min(v):.4f}–{max(v):.4f})" if len(v) > 1 else f"{v[0]:.4f} (one seed)"
GIB_TO_GB = 1024 ** 3 / 1e9
isla435 = mean(r["isla"])
rows435 = [("**ISLA** (384 x 12, 5e-4)", "isla", r["isla"]), ("ISLA, 24 layers (384 x 24, 5e-4)", "r2", R2), ("ISLA at 1e-3 (rate control)", "isla", R1_LR),
           (f"GeoTransolver-256 ({r['gt_rate']}), the recipe width", "gt", r["gt"]), ("GeoTransolver-512 (3e-3), the parameter match", "gt512", GT512),
           ("Transolver-256 (3e-3)", "t", r["t"])]
out = "| configuration at 435 training cars | parameters | surface pressure error, mean (seed range) | ÷ ISLA | step [ms] | peak memory [GB] |\n|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|\n"
ARMN = {"isla": "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "r2": "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused", "gt": "geotransolver_256", "gt512": "geotransolver_512", "t": "transolver_256"}
for lab, ck, v in rows435:
    out += (f"| {lab} | {CS[ARMN[ck]]['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M | {cell(v)} | {mean(v) / isla435:.2f} | {COST[ck][0]:.0f} | "
            f"{COST[ck][1] * GIB_TO_GB:.0f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": The 435-car standing of the DrivAerML Surface task, every configuration at the reporting protocol (200,000 sampled cells per "
      "case, 500 epochs, two seeds, float32 on the 48 validation cars). The ratio is the row's error divided by ISLA's, so a value above "
      "one means ISLA is more accurate than that row. Step time and peak memory are the training step at 200,000 tokens on one GB300 in "
      "bf16 with a batch of one, from the cost sweep of @sec-using-cost, the same instrument for every row. How to read this: "
      "the two GeoTransolver rows differ in what is matched, the recipe width or the parameter count. ISLA leads the first and ties the "
      "second at lower cost. The 24-layer ISLA row is the depth variant the reference selection rejected. Data: "
      "results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json (ISLA, GeoTransolver-512); results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json (GeoTransolver-256, "
      "Transolver); results/cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-435}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-full-data-accuracy
#| output: asis
seeds = lambda v: " and ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in v)
print(f"**The lead is against GeoTransolver at the width the recipe trains, and the parity with its parameter match holds car by "
      f"car.** Both ISLA seeds ({seeds(r['isla'])}) sit below both GeoTransolver-256 seeds ({seeds(r['gt'])}). Against "
      f"GeoTransolver-512 the per-car ratio runs from {PC['per_car_ratio_gt512_over_isla_r1']['p10']:.2f} to "
      f"{PC['per_car_ratio_gt512_over_isla_r1']['p90']:.2f} between the 10th and 90th percentiles, ISLA is the more accurate model on "
      f"{PC['per_car_ratio_gt512_over_isla_r1']['isla_better_count']} of the {PC['n_cars']} cars, and the two models rank the cars alike "
      f"(Spearman correlation of the per-car errors {PC['spearman_isla_r1_gt512']:.2f}; results/drivaer435_percase_2026-09-23.json), so "
      f"what remains at full data is the difficulty of the case rather than the architecture (@sec-shared-floor). Doubling ISLA's depth "
      f"to 24 layers buys {(1 - mean(R2) / mean(r['isla'])) * 100:.1f}% at twice the step time and memory, inside the 1.5% bar the "
      f"reference selection set; the rate control at 1e-3 is {(mean(R1_LR) / mean(r['isla']) - 1) * 100:.0f}% worse than 5e-4 on both "
      "seeds. GeoTransolver's best rate depends on how much data it sees, so the ladder table names its rate on every row; ISLA trains "
      "at 5e-4 on every rung and Transolver at 3e-3.")
```

## The training-car ladder {#sec-car-ladder}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-200k
#| output: asis
out = "| DrivAerML training cars | ISLA (5e-4) | GeoTransolver-256 (better of 1e-3, 3e-3) | Transolver (3e-3) | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA |\n|---:|---|---|---|---:|---:|\n"
for n, rr in CARS.items():
    b = "**" if n == 435 else ""
    out += (f"| {b}{n}{b} | {b}{cell(rr['isla'])}{b} | {b}{cell(rr['gt'])}{b} ({rr['gt_rate']}) | {b}{cell(rr['t'])}{b} "
            f"| {b}{car_ratio[n][0]:.2f}{b} | {b}{car_ratio[n][1]:.2f}{b} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error on the DrivAerML Surface task (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 validation cars): seed mean "
      "(seed range) with every model trained and scored at 200,000 sampled cells per case, ISLA at the reference configuration "
      "(384 wide, 5e-4), GeoTransolver and Transolver at 256 wide, 500 epochs, two seeds. GeoTransolver's column takes the better of its "
      "1e-3 and 3e-3 pairs and names the rate. How to read this: ratios above 1 favor ISLA. The crossover sits between 54 and 109 cars. "
      "The 435-car row is the full training split and the book's primary standing on this task. Data: "
      "results/refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json (27 to 218 cars); results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json (ISLA, 435 cars); "
      "results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json (baselines, 435 cars). {#tbl-scoreboard-200k}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-drivaerml-ladder
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The training-car ladder of the DrivAerML Surface task. Surface-pressure
#|   error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 validation cars) against
#|   the number of training cars, both axes logarithmic, for ISLA (blue
#|   squares), GeoTransolver at its better rate (red circles) and Transolver
#|   (amber triangles); the large marker is the seed mean and the small dots
#|   are the two seeds. How to read this: the red curve sits above the blue
#|   one from 109 cars up and below it at 27 and 54, so the crossover is
#|   between 54 and 109 cars; the curves are joined measurements, not fits
#|   (the fitted law is in @sec-compute-allocation). The x axis spans the
#|   five rungs the ladder has. Data: results/refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json
#|   (27 to 218 cars); results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json (ISLA, 435 cars);
#|   results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json (baselines, 435 cars).
#| code-fold: true
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 4.4))
ns = sorted(CARS)
for key, arm in (("isla_ref", "isla"), ("gt", "gt"), ("t", "t")):
    ax.plot(ns, [mean(CARS[n][arm]) for n in ns], **series_kwargs(key), zorder=3)
    for n in ns:
        ax.plot([n] * len(CARS[n][arm]), CARS[n][arm], ls="none", marker="o", ms=3.2, color=STYLE[key]["color"], zorder=4)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks(ns); ax.set_xticklabels([str(n) for n in ns]); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.set_yticks([0.04, 0.05, 0.06, 0.08, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2]); ax.set_yticklabels(["0.04", "0.05", "0.06", "0.08", "0.1", "0.15", "0.2"])
ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.set_ylim(0.038, 0.2)
ax.set_xlabel("training cars [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure relative L2 error [–]")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_title("DrivAerML Surface task, 200,000 cells per case, 48 validation cars; large marker = seed mean, dots = seeds")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-200k-reading
#| output: asis
tr = [car_ratio[n][1] for n in ns]
g27, g54, g109 = (car_ratio[n][0] for n in (27, 54, 109))
print(f"**GeoTransolver's small-data lead is an offset, not a slope.** It leads ISLA by {pct(g27)} at 27 cars and {pct(g54)} at 54; ISLA "
      f"leads by {pct(g109)} at 109, {pct(car_ratio[218][0])} at 218 and {pct(car_ratio[435][0])} at 435, and Transolver ÷ ISLA stays "
      f"between {min(tr):.2f} and {max(tr):.2f} on every rung. The learning-curve exponent over 27 to 218 cars is "
      f"{RBX['isla_r1']['exponent']:.2f} for ISLA against {RBX['gt256_lr3e3']['exponent']:.2f} for GeoTransolver-256 at 3e-3 "
      f"({RBX['gt256']['exponent']:.2f} at 1e-3, from a worse start) and {RBX['transolver256']['exponent']:.2f} for Transolver, and the "
      "fitted law of @sec-compute-allocation gives the two architectures the same case exponent within the bootstrap. Above 100,000 cells "
      "per case the error of every model is flat in the cell count (@sec-equal-budget), so the 200,000-cell protocol is a converged "
      "budget on this task; below it an independent draw of a car's surface is a noisy instrument, and the stratified sampler of "
      "@sec-using-sampler removes most of that noise at a fixed budget.")
```

## What this standing does not say {#sec-surface-limits}

**The lead is one dataset, one task and one metric, measured in
distribution.** Its scope, the controls behind it and the decisions the
validation set entered are in @sec-limits. The wing standings, where both
baselines lead, are @sec-data-efficiency.
